pointers.sentence: A `Signer` takes keyword arguments only (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.__init__`).
The documentation states the rule as a separator outside the URL-safe base64 alphabet (`docs/topics/signing.txt`).
`Signer.signature` calls `base64_hmac` with the signer's salt followed by `"signer"`, the value, the signer's key (or one passed to it) and the algorithm (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.signature`).
`Signer.unsign` reverses it (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.unsign`).

`TimestampSigner.timestamp` is the current time in whole seconds since the epoch, written in base 62, and `TimestampSigner.sign` appends the separator and the timestamp to the value before passing it to `Signer.sign`, so the signature covers the time as well (`django/core/signing.py:TimestampSigner.sign`).

It splits off the timestamp and decodes it, and if given a maximum age, as seconds or a timedelta, raises `SignatureExpired` when more seconds than that have passed (`django/core/signing.py:TimestampSigner.unsign`).
`Signer.sign_object` signs a value of any type its serializer can write, not only a string (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.sign_object`).

`Signer.unsign_object` calls `unsign` first, passing a maximum age on to a `TimestampSigner`, and only then looks for the `"."`, decodes the base64 and decompresses: nothing is decompressed that the key did not sign (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.unsign_object`).
`JSONSerializer` writes JSON with no spaces after `","` and `":"`, encoded as Latin-1, and reads it back the same way (`django/core/signing.py:JSONSerializer`).
The documentation's reason for JSON: even if `SECRET_KEY` is stolen, an attacker cannot run commands through it as through the pickle format (`docs/topics/signing.txt`).

`dumps` makes a `TimestampSigner` from its key and salt and returns its `sign_object` of the value; `loads` makes one from its key, salt and fallback keys and returns its `unsign_object` of the string (`django/core/signing.py:dumps`, `django/core/signing.py:loads`).

`dumps` makes a `TimestampSigner` from its key and salt and returns its `sign_object` of the value; `loads` makes one from its key, salt and fallback keys and returns its `unsign_object` of the string (`django/core/signing.py:dumps`, `django/core/signing.py:loads`).
The documentation's reason: a salt is a namespace, and a string signed in one is refused by code that checks in another (`docs/topics/signing.txt`).
`b64_encode` is URL-safe base64 with the trailing `"="` padding stripped, and `b64_decode` restores the padding before decoding (`django/core/signing.py:b64_decode`).
`b62_encode` and `b62_decode` write and read an integer in the digits and letters of `BASE62_ALPHABET`, with a `"-"` in front of a negative one (`django/core/signing.py:b62_encode`).

Called with no algorithm, `base64_hmac` warns with `RemovedInDjango2028Warning` and uses `"sha1"`; in Django 2028 its default becomes `"sha256"`, as does that of `salted_hmac` (`django/core/signing.py:base64_hmac`).
`get_cookie_signer` makes the signer for cookies (`django/core/signing.py:get_cookie_signer`).

`SessionBase.decode` reads it with `loads` and no maximum age; on a `BadSignature` it logs the warning `"Session data corrupted"` to `"django.security.SuspiciousSession"`, and on any failure returns an empty session (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.encode`, `django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.decode`).

`SessionBase.decode` reads it with `loads` and no maximum age; on a `BadSignature` it logs the warning `"Session data corrupted"` to `"django.security.SuspiciousSession"`, and on any failure returns an empty session (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.encode`, `django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.decode`).

In the backend that keeps the whole session in the cookie, the session key is itself the string `dumps` makes of the session, compressed, with the salt `"django.contrib.sessions.backends.signed_cookies"` (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/signed_cookies.py:SessionStore`).

The messages' `CookieStorage` signs through `get_cookie_signer` with the salt `"django.contrib.messages"`, using `sign_object` with compression and `unsign_object` with no maximum age (`django/contrib/messages/storage/cookie.py:CookieStorage.__init__`).
